question: What is the arithmetic mean of 10, 12, 23, 23, 16, 23, 21, 16?
answer:
The core built-in types are int (whole numbers), float (decimal numbers), str (text), bool (True or False) and NoneType (the single value None, meaning "no value"). [S1] Write a function average(numbers) that returns the arithmetic mean of a list. [S2]

**Computed results:** sum([10, 12, 23, 23, 16, 23, 21, 16]) / 8 = 18 [C1]

citations.title: Python Lecture Notes
citations.text: 1. Variables and Data Types A variable is a name that refers to a value stored in memory. In Python you create a variable by assignment, for example age = 21. Python is dynamically typed: the type belongs to the value, not to the name, so the same name can later refer to a string. The core built-in types are int (whole numbers), float (decimal numbers), str (text), bool (True or False) and NoneType (the single value None, meaning "no value"). The function type(x) reports the type of x. Conversion functions such as int("42"), float("3.5") and str(10) create new values of another type; int("abc") raises a ValueError. Strings are immutable sequences of characters. Indexing starts at zero, so "python"[0] is "p", and negative indexes count from the end, so "python"[-1] is "n". Slicing "python"[1:4] returns "yth" (start included, stop excluded).

citations.title: Python Exercise Guide
citations.text:
Exercise Set B: Functions and Collections
Exercise B1. Write a function average(numbers) that returns the arithmetic mean of a list. Handle an empty list by returning None instead of dividing by zero.
Exercise B2. Count word frequency. Given a sentence, build a dictionary mapping each lowercase word to its count. Use counts[word] = counts.get(word, 0) + 1. Alternative: collections.Counter.
Exercise B3. Remove duplicates from a list while preserving order. Converting to a set removes duplicates but loses ordering; use a seen set and an output list, or dict.fromkeys(items).
Exercise B4. Explain why the following function is buggy: def add_item(item, items=[]): items.append(item); return items. Answer: the default list is created once and shared between calls, so items accumulate across calls. The fix is to use None as the default.

S4.title: Python Glossary Overloaded Terms
S4.text: program prints the same random numbers on every run. iterable: an object you can loop over, such as a list or string.  An iterator is the object that produces the values one at a time and is returned by iter(iterable). generator: a function that uses yield to produce values lazily, one at a time, instead of building a whole list in memory. decorator: a function that wraps another function; written with the @ syntax above a def line. mean: Python has no built-in mean. Use statistics.mean(data), or statistics.fmean(data) for a faster floating-point mean.

S5.title: Python Reference Notes
S5.text:
BUILT-IN FUNCTIONS
len(x) returns the number of items in x.
sum(nums) adds the numbers in an iterable.
min(nums) and max(nums) return the smallest and largest items.
sorted(items) returns a new sorted list; list.sort() sorts in place and returns None.
enumerate(items) gives (index, item) pairs.
zip(a, b) pairs items from two iterables and stops at the shortest.
range(stop) generates 0 .. stop-1; range(start, stop, step) supports steps.
isinstance(x, int) tests whether x is an instance of a type.
